key_insight: The paper computes steady lid-driven cavity flows with a linearized iterative solver and tests their stability by checking eigenvalues of the discretized perturbation problem.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to assess when high-Reynolds-number cavity-flow solutions are physically reliable or unstable in finite-element simulations.
method: Linearize the nonlinear convective terms and solve a sequence of linear steady-state problems.
Apply small perturbations to the steady velocity and pressure fields and linearize the perturbation equations.
Discretize on triangular finite-element meshes and solve the resulting generalized eigenvalue problem.
evidence_signal: Stability was evaluated on a sequence of refined meshes across multiple Reynolds numbers for square-cavity flow, using the presence of eigenvalues with positive real part as the instability criterion.
watch_item: Stability conclusions depend on mesh refinement and eigenvalue accuracy, so coarse discretization may miss critical unstable modes.
paper_title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
